newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan unveils strict election code.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan unveils strict election code.

text.p: Pakistan's President Farooq Leghari decreed strict rules on Thursday for politicians contesting national and provincial polls set for February 3.
"The whole idea is that good people should win the elections," caretaker Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Fakhruddin Ibrahim told a news conference.

He said that under the ordinance each candidate would have to declare that he is not a loan defaulter or tax evader and state his educational qualifications and occupation. He would have to declare details of taxes he had paid in recent years.

Ibrahim said candidates could be barred from standing, and winning candidates could be dismissed, if found to have given false or incorrect information. In such cases they could be jailed for five years and fined 100,000 rupees ($2,500).
Ibrahim said information provided by candidates and parties before the elections would be open for public scrutiny.
"You can now understand how strict it would be," he said. "People were saying that the wrong kind of people come to the assemblies. We don't want the wrong kind of people to come."
He said candidates would be barred from changing their party after winning elections and from voting against party orders.
Ibrahim said parties would have to disclose their election expenses and contributions within 30 days after the polls.
Candidates for the National Assembly (lower house) would be allowed to spend no more than a million rupees on their campaign and candidates for provincial assemblies no more than 600,000.

President Farooq Leghari dismissed prime minister Benazir Bhutto on charges of corruption and misrule, and dissolved the National Assembly on November 5. He named a caretaker government under Meraj Khalid to supervise elections on February 3.
